author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Rents out AI computing power. Now a public company.
what_it_does: CoreWeave operates data centres full of graphics processors and rents that capacity to AI companies. It started in cryptocurrency mining and converted to AI computing. It listed publicly in 2025, which makes it the only company in this coverage with audited quarterly disclosure.
how_it_makes_money: Long-term contracts for guaranteed compute capacity, plus shorter-term usage. Contracts are large, long and concentrated among a few customers.
why_it_matters: It is the readable proxy for the whole private AI complex. Because it files publicly, its disclosures reveal things about its customers and about AI infrastructure economics that private peers never publish.
competitive_position: Competes with Amazon, Microsoft and Google, who are also partly its customers and its suppliers, and with other specialist providers.
key_risks: Revenue is heavily concentrated in a small number of customers.
Very high debt taken on to fund data centre construction.
The processors it buys depreciate quickly and may lose value faster than expected.
If AI demand slows, the fixed costs do not.

glossary.definition: A graphics processor. Originally for rendering images, now the standard hardware for training AI models.
A contract where the customer pays for capacity whether or not they use it.
